result_text:
Promotions now carry an optional description, and it comes back from all six promotion queries and from `createPromotion`. The full suite passes (607 tests), and a temporary round-trip test I wrote and then deleted confirmed the text for SUMMER and `null` for a promotion created without one.

What changed, in the three files you named:

- **`model/Promotion.java`**: added a `description` component as the last field of the record. I also kept the old six-argument constructor, which sets the description to `null`, so `PromotionService` compiles unchanged.
- **`schema.sql`**: added a nullable `description VARCHAR(255)` column to `promotion`.
- **`DataStore.java`**: `createPromotion` inserts the description. `findPromotionByCode`, `listPromotionsActiveOn`, `listPromotionsActiveOnInRegion`, `listPromotionsByCategory`, `findBestPromotion` and `listUnusedPromotions` select it and pass it into the record.

One gap to decide on: the description can only be set by passing a seven-argument `Promotion` directly to `DataStore.createPromotion`. `PromotionService.createPromotion(code, discount, start, end, category)` has no description parameter, so promotions created through the service always get none. Adding that parameter would mean touching `PromotionService.java`, which was outside the files you listed. I left it alone; say the word if you want it.

I did not commit anything.
